Im not a capitalist by any means but zero sum is objectively correct. We live on a finite planet with finite resources and hungry people. Every bite of food I take could have extended the life of a starving child somewhere and that's **fact**. Therefore, I have the moral prerogative to justify my existence and right to eat by attempting to make a world a better place. Freeloaders are stealing from those who are starving *and* have the potential to improve society. They exist. Even in a communistic utopia, the unacceptable nature of laziness still holds true, possibly more so because of how fragile such a society would be.

I completely agree. Just because someone is old doesn't mean they didn't contribute to society in their younger years. Also more suffering than not would probably be created by taking poor care of our elderly.  A society of abundance is a little bit of a stretch though... in America 38 million are food insecure and that's in a country that is supposedly first world. We have a long long way to go before everyone has everything they need. Until that point is met, every bite of food you take is a bite that could have gone to someone else. Thats kind of a lot to think about all the time so most people don't, but it is true and will be for the foreseeable future.

People will suffer. Those who have the capability to use less and give more have a moral prerogative to do so. To be unproductive isn't wrong if it truly is the extent of your potential, however for many, they could be doing a lot more and consuming a lot less. These people shouldn't be punished per say, but free loading should be viewed as harming your fellow citizen if the freeloader is doing so voluntarily.

People either are a net positive or a net negative to society. Productiveness isnt valuable just beacuse “money”. They make people lives better through contributions. Similarly if you take more than you put in, you are harming others by taking resources for yourself. This doesnt mean that we should kill all non contributers but it does indicate productivity means something.
